title: Manna Bookshop
subject: Criminal Law & Procedure
stem:
Question ID: 14680_manna_bookshop

In a jurisdiction that has abolished the felony-murder rule, but otherwise follows the common law of murder, Peter and Mary, both armed with automatic weapons, went into a privately owned Christian bookstore, Manna & Margins, to rob it. Peter ordered all the customers and employees in the bookstore to lie on the floor. When some were slow to obey, Mary, not intending to hit anyone, fired about 15 rounds toward the high ceiling. One round ricocheted off a stone column near a display of study Bibles and struck and killed Lydia, a customer in the bookstore. Peter and Mary were charged with murder of Lydia.

Which of the following is correct?
call: Which of the following is correct?

choices.A: Mary can be convicted of murder, because she did the act of killing, but Peter cannot be convicted of either murder or manslaughter.
choices.B: Both can be convicted only of manslaughter, because the killing was unintentional.
choices.C: Mary can be convicted of murder, but Peter can be convicted only of manslaughter because he did not fire the fatal shot.
choices.D: Both can be convicted of murder.

rightExplanation:
D is correct.

Gold Key: Felony-murder abolition does not erase common-law murder. An unintentional killing can still be murder when the killer’s conduct shows extreme recklessness toward human life.

Gold Key: Accomplice liability does not stop at the person who fired the fatal shot. A partner in the armed robbery can be liable for the foreseeable murder committed during the joint venture.

Silver Key: Read the answer array on two axes: the shooter’s homicide grade and the partner’s derivative liability. The credited answer is the only choice that gets both axes right.

Mary fired about 15 rounds in a crowded bookstore. Even though she did not intend to hit anyone, that act supports murder through malice based on extreme recklessness. Peter joined the armed robbery, ordered people to the floor, and participated in the dangerous armed venture. The shooting and resulting death were foreseeable in that setup. Both can be convicted of murder.

wrongExplanations.A: This is the dominant trap. It gets Mary’s side mostly right, then cuts Peter out entirely because he did not fire. Gold Key: accomplice liability does not stop at the trigger-puller when the resulting crime was foreseeable during the joint armed robbery.
wrongExplanations.B: This answer treats “unintentional” as an automatic downgrade to manslaughter. Gold Key: unintentional homicide can still be murder if the conduct shows extreme reckless indifference to human life. The felony-murder abolition fact does not eliminate that independent murder route.
wrongExplanations.C: This answer recognizes that Peter can be liable, but it downgrades him because he did not fire the fatal shot. Silver Key: do not grade liability by who pulled the trigger. In this array, the partner-liability axis asks whether Peter rides with the foreseeable murder, not whether he personally fired.

studentScript: Two axes. Mary fired many rounds in a crowded place, so Gold Key one makes murder possible even without intent to hit. Peter was part of the armed robbery, so Gold Key two keeps him on the foreseeable murder. A erases Peter, B downgrades everyone, C downgrades Peter. D keeps both layers.

A.signal: The choice uses the act-of-killing fact as if it ends the whole question. It gives a right-looking answer for Mary but wipes out Peter's partner-liability axis.
A.lawyer: Mary can be convicted of murder; Peter is not erased merely because he did not fire. Accomplice liability can attach to foreseeable crimes committed in the joint armed robbery.

B.signal: The answer turns one visible fact, no intent to hit anyone, into a complete homicide-grade rule. The student needs the depraved-heart Gold Key to cut it cleanly.
B.lawyer: Unintentional killings can be murder when malice is supplied by extreme reckless indifference to human life.

C.signal: The choice focuses on Peter not firing the fatal shot. That fact is visible, but it is not the deciding element once the accomplice-liability axis is in play.
C.lawyer: A non-shooter accomplice may be liable for the same murder when the killing was a foreseeable crime in the jointly aided armed robbery.

D.signal: This is the residual that preserves both layers: Mary murder through reckless malice, Peter murder through accomplice scope.
D.lawyer: Both can be convicted of murder under the supplied common-law murder and accomplice-liability frame.

remediation.title: Do not stop at felony-murder abolition
remediation.signal: Stem says felony murder abolished, but answer choices still ask murder/manslaughter for both actors.
remediation.studentMove: Check both axes: murder grade and accomplice scope.
remediation.tinyRule: Abolishing felony murder removes one route to murder, not all murder.
remediation.trap: Downgrading to manslaughter because the death was unintentional.
